key_insight: CLExEval shows that fluent LLM explanations can look clinically convincing even when the final diagnosis is wrong, so reasoning quality and answer accuracy must be evaluated separately.
clinical_relevance: For clinical NLP, this framework highlights that automated model evaluation can overestimate real-world reliability unless expert-verified checks are included.
method: Human-in-the-loop evaluation of LLM clinical reasoning
Progressive information masking across 40 rare diagnostic cases
Expert physician annotation of 5,600 items plus 200 reasoning traces
evidence_signal: Across the abstract’s reported tests, GPT-4o-mini fell from 95.0% to 32.5% accuracy under information scarcity, and LLM-as-a-Judge approved 47.9% of clinically incorrect outputs in a human-verified failure set of 142.
watch_item: The results come from rare-case, expert-annotated evaluations, so broader generalization to routine clinical settings and other model families still needs validation.
paper_title: CLExEval: A Human-in-the-Loop Framework for Qualitative Evaluation of LLM Clinical Reasoning
